question: Can TypeScript avoid unnecessary adaptive prediction at the general_element_part argument loop without changing parser behavior?
hypothesis: Guarding decision 2985 with the FIRST token of function_argument will avoid prediction when the only valid loop action is exit, while retaining adaptive prediction when caller context matters.
selection: Complete frozen 1,244-file opaque production corpus; tail statistics reuse the 12 opaque ids selected by experiment 004.
candidate: Post-process the generated TypeScript general_element_part loop so adaptivePredict runs only when lookahead is LEFT_PAREN.
acceptance: The 12-file tail has a repeatable parser-core reduction.
The complete corpus has no token, diagnostic, prediction-mode, or fallback-attempt differences in any repetition.
Function-argument parse contexts remain unchanged, including adjacent argument groups.
Only opaque file identities and hashes leave the private corpus.
limitations: The deterministic bootstrap interval has only three samples and is descriptive.
The laboratory has no production semantic indexer; unchanged parse-tree construction is the semantic-consumer boundary.
Java remains an unmodified control and does not include the TypeScript generated-code optimization.
